item.text: {"text":"The 2024–2026 search found related text–interaction alignment work, but no verified exact match combining GRU4Rec, a text encoder trained from scratch, and joint contrastive training. CLA-Rec (ICDM 2024) aligns LLM-derived description embeddings with collaborative representations, then uses a Transformer sequence encoder. CALRec (RecSys 2024) combines recommendation and contrastive objectives around pretrained PaLM-2. CTT (KDD 2025) uses BERT-base text embeddings and a Transformer. These support investigating semantic alignment, but their pretrained encoders and backbones do not satisfy this experiment’s constraints. Sources: [CLA-Rec](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10884256/), [CALRec](https://research.google/pubs/calrec-contrastive-alignment-of-generative-llms-for-sequential-recommendation/), [CTT](https://csse.szu.edu.cn/attachment/cglr/1756969546_Conference-25-KDD-CTT.pdf).\n\nA constraint-compatible hypothesis—not an established result from these papers—is one GRU4Rec network with randomly initialized token embeddings, mean-pooled title/description tokens, and a small projection jointly trained with item-ID embeddings. Fuse text and ID representations inside the network; optimize next-item prediction plus a lightly weighted item-ID/text contrastive loss. Use only observed training text, mask missing descriptions, and exclude repeated item IDs from contrastive negatives. This preserves one jointly trained predictor per category without external weights or separate scoring models. Older [EC4SRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.01347) reports contrastive-learning benefits with GRU4Rec, supporting backbone compatibility, but does not establish that scratch-trained text features will improve this benchmark."}
